root_cause_label: Insufficient Skip-Gram Pair Generation (Single Random Offset per Position) Yields Semantically Incoherent Embeddings
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent implemented skip-gram training that samples only one random context offset per center word instead of all window positions, producing a vastly under-trained embedding space where analogy evaluation persistently returns input words themselves across all recovery attempts.
t_err_evidence: creates word2vec2.py with flawed on-the-fly pair sampling that yields poor embeddings
t_commit_evidence: Step 14 executes the full 3-epoch training run using train.py with the flawed single-offset sampling strategy. After this run completes (confirmed in step 15 terminal output showing loss ~9-10 and files saved), the core embedding parameters reflect the defective learning approach. All subsequent training builds incrementally on this base without correcting the fundamental pair-generation design.
t_surface_evidence: king - man + woman ≈ man; paris - france + england ≈ england
trigger_explanation: The agent lacks the domain knowledge that skip-gram training requires pairing each center word with ALL words in its context window (producing window_size*2 pairs per position). Instead it samples a single random offset per position, which is analogous to training with a window size of 1 on a random subset of positions — massively reducing the learning signal compared to standard word2vec. The agent never recognizes this architectural deficiency, attributing poor analogy results to insufficient epochs or learning rate rather than the pair-generation design.
